Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that APG4RecSim achieves the best overall performance on discrimination, ranking, and rating tasks, improving ranking quality by up to 7% in nDCG@10 and reducing rating distribution divergence by 8% in JSD compared to existing profile-generation baselines. Beyond overall performance gains, our results show that APG4RecSim produces profiles that are resilient to popularity- and position-induced biases and maintain stable performance across datasets and different LLMs.
keyword: recommender system, large language model, generative agents

title: Poster: Car2Vec: Task-Agnostic Latent Embeddings from CAN Bus for Efficient V2X Communication
abstract: The high bandwidth demand of raw sensor data transmission remains a critical bottleneck for scalable Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks. We propose Car2Vec - a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that generates compact latent embeddings from vehicle CAN bus data. Our initial experiments demonstrate the framework's ability to create visually distinguishable embeddings in latent space, successfully separating clusters for fuel from different suppliers and identifying varying levels of motor oil viscosity. These early results suggest the framework's potential to encode semantic state information including vehicle dynamics and driver context, and serve as efficient communication primitives for V2V/V2I applications, potentially reducing wireless overhead by orders of magnitude compared to raw telemetry. By moving computation to vehicle edge devices, Car2Vec aligns with the AI-RAN co-design vision, offering a promising direction for semantic-aware resource optimization in next-gen transportation networks.
keyword: vehicle-to-everything, embeddings, contrastive learning, AI-RAN

title: Modelling and Solving Problems in Communications and Network Security Elegantly Using a Unified Framework for Intelligence and Intelligent Systems
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern communication networks and security systems demands intelligent solutions that can adapt to dynamic threats while maintaining operational constraints. This paper presents Constrained Object Hierarchies (COH), a neuroscience-grounded theoretical framework for artificial general intelligence that provides a unified approach to modeling and implementing intelligent systems. We demonstrate COH's efficacy through five comprehensive case studies in communications and network security: Intelligent Zero-Trust Network Access Controller, Autonomous Cyber Deception System, Self-Healing Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN), AI-Powered Network Intrusion Detection System, and Dynamic Security Group Micro-Segmentation Planner. Each system is formally modeled using the COH 9-tuple representation and implemented using the GISMOL (General Intelligent System Modelling Language) toolkit. Our results show that COH enables elegant modeling of complex security systems while maintaining constraint awareness, hierarchical reasoning, and adaptive intelligence. The framework bridges the gap between theoretical modeling and practical implementation, providing a systematic methodology for developing intelligent systems that can reason about constraints, learn from experience, and maintain security guarantees in dynamic environments.
keyword: Artificial General Intelligence, Artificial General Intelligence, Communications, Constrained Object Hierarchies, Cyber Deception, GISMOL, Intelligent Systems, Network Security, SD-WAN, Zero-Trust

title: A Robust Horizontal Federated Learning Framework Based on Trimmed K-Means and Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: To address the challenges of model degradation and security threats caused by data heterogeneity and poisoning attacks in Horizontal Federated Learning, this paper proposes a robust and privacy-preserving horizontal federated learning framework based on Trimmed K-Means clustering and Homomorphic Encryption. The proposed method replaces traditional K-Means with a Trimmed K-Means algorithm to achieve robust local outlier detection, mitigating the distortion of cluster centers caused by malicious data. Each client performs local anomaly filtering and applies the Paillier Homomorphic Encryption scheme to encrypt its gradient updates, ensuring privacy preservation during communication and aggregation. On the server side, a Dynamic Trust Evaluation Mechanism is introduced to continuously assess the reliability of participating clients through temporal trust evolution and cluster consistency analysis. The framework further employs robust aggregation algorithms to replace conventional averaging, thereby enhancing resilience against coordinated poisoning and adversarial updates. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains over 90% detection accuracy and less than 3% performance degradation even when up to 40% of clients are malicious, significantly outperforming traditional clustering-based evaluation schemes. This work effectively enhances the robustness, security, and trustworthiness of federated learning systems under adversarial and privacy-sensitive environments.
keyword: Dynamic Trust Evaluation, Homomorphic Encryption, Horizontal Federated Learning, Trimmed K-Means

title: BlockEdge: A Hybrid Blockchain Framework for Secure and Efficient Collaboration in EEC Environments
abstract: In End-Edge-Cloud (EEC) computing environments, the diversity of devices often requires cloud-trained models to be adapted for end/edge devices, complicating decentralized project management. To address this, end/edge devices are increasingly using local model sharing instead of traditional cloud solutions. Popular platforms like GitHub and DockerHub lack the necessary data authenticity and security for high-stakes applications. While blockchain can ensure secure data sharing, permissioned blockchains struggle with the dynamic nature of EEC devices. To solve this, we propose BlockEdge, a hybrid blockchain architecture combining a permissioned blockchain with Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) for cloud-based data management and a permissionless blockchain with Proof of Work (PoW) for decentralized model sharing at the end/edge. We enhance the PoW process with a dynamic mining algorithm and a lazy-loading Merkle tree structure, improving energy efficiency and computational performance. Experimental results show that BlockEdge reduces energy consumption by over 50% and cuts data update time by 91.73%, effectively addressing the energy and time inefficiencies of mainstream consensus mechanisms.
keyword: AI, blockchain, end-edge-cloud, heterogeneous computing, optimization algorithms

title: Demo: Exploring Time Series Data from Massive Sensor Systems through Change Point Correlation
abstract: Complex cyber-physical systems such as power plants and buildings are monitored by large-scale distributed sensor systems. Each sensor produces measurements in the form of time series, resulting in massive collections of time series data. Domain experts such as engineers use these collections for performance monitoring, maintenance operations, root-cause analysis, and optimization. Due to the sheer volume of data, it is often necessary to select a small subset of the data for extended analysis and continuous monitoring. However, selecting this subset requires metadata that is both available and informative, extensive knowledge about the available signals, and the general functional structure of the facility. In the context of complex systems with massive and highly customized sensor configurations that produce extremely heterogeneous measurements, identifying time series of interest or groups of functionally related time series is a difficult and time-consuming task. In this paper, we demonstrate how Change Point Correlation helps to uncover functional structure and can be used to explore massive sensor systems using only the raw time series data without relying on extensive metadata. Our application allows interactive exploration of hundreds of time series, each consisting of thousands of samples, and supports the extraction of functional subgroups for further analysis, as well as the discovery of related time series, isolated changes, and events for root-cause analysis.
keyword: sensor systems, change point detection, time series, data mining

title: A Software Architecture for Real-Time Digital Twins in Machining
abstract: Digital twins are increasingly recognized as a key enabler for optimizing complex systems by providing virtual representations that are continuously updated with real-world data. To unlock their full potential, real-time capabilities are essential, ensuring that decision-making, monitoring, and control can be performed with minimal latency. However, previous work has mainly concentrated on offline analysis or loosely coupled synchronization, leaving the systematic design of scalable and reliable real-time digital twins insufficiently addressed. In this paper we introduce a reference architecture for implementing real-time digital twins, covering requirements such as data acquisition, integration, synchronization, and processing, and highlighting enabling technologies that support low-latency and dependable operations. To validate this approach, we developed a prototype framework and applied it to a machine tool case study, demonstrating how real-time synchronization and decision support can be achieved in practice. The results show that our framework enables consistent, high-frequency interaction between physical and virtual assets, providing a foundation for advanced applications in monitoring, control, and optimization of manufacturing systems.
keyword: Digital Twin, real-time, Software Architecture, Virtual Commissioning

title: Infrastructure-Free Indoor Occupancy Estimation via Passive BLE Scanning
abstract: Accurately estimating indoor occupancy is fundamental to the development of modern smart buildings, which aim to optimize critical parameters such as Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) control, safety, and resource management in real time to reduce energy waste. Traditional sensing approaches, including cameras, Passive Infrared (PIR) sensors, and CO 2 monitors, often encounter high deployment costs, maintenance overhead, and significant privacy concerns, particularly under General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) regulations. This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a non-invasive occupancy estimation system that exclusively relies on Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) scans performed via a mobile device, eliminating the need for prior structural information or dedicated sensing infrastructure. The proposed method analyzes statistical differences between various university environments, such as Laboratories , Classrooms , and Corridors , while integrating variables such as the number of fixed and mobile devices, the average device density per person, and the interference caused by signal bleed-through between adjacent rooms.
keyword: Indoor Occupancy Estimation, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Passive Human Sensing, Infrastructure-Free Sensing, Context-Aware Modeling, Smart Buildings, Snapshot-Based Estimation

title: Improving the Convergence and Diversity of Evolutionary Algorithms in Biobjective Optimization Problems
abstract: Multiobjective optimization problems require algorithms capable of efficiently approximating the Pareto optimal front while ensuring good convergence and diversity. In this paper, we introduce and analyze two approaches designed to refine the search process in the later stages of evolutionary multiobjective optimization algorithms. Our proposal takes an approximation of the Pareto optimal front for a multiobjective optimization problem. Then, it defines different subregions, reference points, and weight vectors, to better converge to the true Pareto optimal front. We propose two approaches: (1) defining subregions based on objective space partitioning and (2) dynamically adapting weight vectors distributions based on the front's geometry. These strategies allow for a more precise approximation of the Pareto optimal front while maintaining a well-distributed set of solutions.
keyword: population-based multiobjective optimization algorithms, achievement scalarizing function, adaptation weight vectors, reference points

title: AI-Enhanced Guided-Inquiry Platform for Collaborative Learning in Introductory Programming
abstract: This paper presents a digital learning framework, coLearn-AI (hereafter referred to as the system), that combines guided inquiry pedagogy with intelligent, adaptive feedback mechanisms to support collaborative learning in introductory programming courses. The system enables instructors to author structured inquiry activities, manage student groups, and provide embedded AI guidance that scaffolds learning in real time. Students work in groups and engage with progressively complex problems through exploration, collaboration, and reflection. The system integrates synchronous collaborative workspaces, turn-taking mechanisms, and analytics dashboards that help instructors monitor student progress at scale. A key innovation is the integration of AI-driven formative feedback (OpenAI API is used), where instructors embed AI guidance directives within activity files. These directives, visible only to instructors, enable the AI module to provide context-aware feedback that aligns with pedagogical goals. By bridging structured human facilitation with adaptive, intelligent tutoring capabilities, the system promotes engagement, accountability, and deeper conceptual understanding. The platform has been successfully deployed in multiple university courses for in-class work since September 2025; instructors monitor progress through dashboards. We report implementation status and early classroom use. This paper describes the pedagogical foundations, system architecture, activity model, AI feedback pipeline, and group-learning mechanisms and outlines directions for formal efficiency evaluation and refinement.

subfield_name: Theory and algorithms for application domains
title: Robustly Learning Mixtures of k Arbitrary Gaussians
abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for the problem of robustly estimating a mixture of k arbitrary Gaussians in ? d , for any fixed k , in the presence of a constant fraction of arbitrary corruptions. This resolves the main open problem in several previous works on algorithmic robust statistics, which addressed the special cases of robustly estimating (a) a single Gaussian, (b) a mixture of TV-distance separated Gaussians, and (c) a uniform mixture of two Gaussians. Our main tools are an efficient partial clustering algorithm that relies on the sum-of-squares method, and a novel tensor decomposition algorithm that allows errors in both Frobenius norm and low-rank terms.
keyword: Gaussian Mixture Model, Robust Statistics, Tensor Decomposition, Sum-of-Squares

title: Poster: Detecting Hidden Cameras using LED Illumination Sweeps
abstract: We present SweepLED , a practical hidden-camera detection system that augments a smartphone with a LED-embedded case. SweepLED performs a sequence of multi-angle LED illumination while the user simply holds the phone still, allowing the smartphone camera to capture reflection changes caused by illumination variation. By analyzing the reflection, SweepLED distinguishes hidden camera lenses from ordinary reflective objects. Our prototype demonstrates that SweepLED can accurately detect hidden cameras in realistic environments, achieving approximately 94% detection accuracy with a sweep time of under 5 seconds.
keyword: hidden camera detection, privacy, smartphone

title: Smart AgroChain-CN: An IoT-Driven Framework for Real-Time Agricultural Supply Chain Monitoring and Economic Efficiency Assessment in China
abstract: Digitization in the Chinese agricultural sector is being utilized in order to overcome food security, logistics inefficiencies and rural income inequality. The paper presents Smart AgroChain-CN, a single Internet-of-Things (IoT) platform through which the agricultural supply chain will have the end-to-end visibility and data-driven economic-efficiency analysis. There are three layers of IoT sensing, hybrid LoRa-5G networking, and cloud-based analytics in the framework to monitor production, storage, and distribution in real-time. There is the suggestion of a composite Economic Efficiency Index (EEI), which determines the financial and operational gains. A pilot project integrated in Jiangsu Province shows implementation of less delay in delivery (39.7%), less post-harvest loss (46%), and less cost of logistics (33%) as compared to the traditional operations. The research provides a scalable data-centric agri-logistics management model that can be applicable to other upcoming economies.
keyword: China, IoT architecture, economic efficiency, smart agriculture, supply-chain analytics

title: A Trust Assessment Method for Photovoltaic Data Based on Multi-Layer Edge Computing
abstract: Power system is one of the national infrastructures, which is crucial for the development of the country's livelihood and economy. The transmission of photovoltaic data faces security threats in data collection, data routing, and business execution, mainly tampering and stealing of photovoltaic data. This paper proposes a multi-layer trust assessment model that utilizes trust assessment techniques to calculate the trust of PV system nodes as well as data within a certain range In this paper, the architecture is divided into four layers, which are the data collection layer, the edge layer, the routing layer, and the cloud computing layer, and proposes a trust assessment methodology for the first three layers of nodes.
keyword: Cybersecurity, Data Security, Edge Cloud Networks, Photovoltaic Data, Trust assessment

title: Human-centric Evaluation of Semantic Resources: A Systematic Mapping Study
abstract: Semantic resources such as ontologies and knowledge graphs enable intelligent applications in a broad range of application areas. As ensuring their quality is important, evaluation activities are an integral part of their life-cycle. Yet, several aspects of these resources, such as domain or modelling correctness, are not amenable to automatic evaluation and require assessment through human participation. Despite such human-centric evaluation of semantic resources (HESR) is essential, there is a lack of a systematic understanding of this area in terms of a theoretical framework as well as an overview of concrete HESR approaches and trends . We address this gap by, firstly, integrating existing literature into a theoretical framework for defining and characterising HESR thus developing a new perspective on this area. Second, we perform a Systematic Mapping Study of 15 years of work published in this area covering 144 papers in order to empirically ground and extend the theoretical framework and identify trends and best practices. These theoretical foundations , insights into current trends and practices as well as our openly available data and analysis scripts aim to enable new research in this area and offer practical guidelines for performing HESR to researchers and practitioners alike.
keyword: Semantic web, semantic resources, linked data, knowledge graphs, human-centric evaluation

title: Rediscovering Collaborative Whiteboarding for Problem Solving in the Era of AI
abstract: As AI tools continue to improve automated code generation, CS educators must ensure that students develop problem-solving skills of their own. This work presents collaborative whiteboard-based activities used in an Introduction to Data Structures course. Through these hands-on activities, students work together to reveal and address their conceptual gaps while building their problem-solving abilities.

title: Ariadne?an adaptive router for fault-tolerant multicomputers
abstract: Adaptive routing has been proposed as a means of improving performance and fault-tolerance in multicomputer networks. While a number of algorithms have been proposed, few adaptive routers have been implemented in hardware. This paper presents the design and implementation of Ariadne --- a prototype single chip, hardware router. The primary motivation is tolerance to link and router failures, while reconciling conflicting demands on performance. This is achieved by implementing the m -misroute backtracking protocol (MB- m ) using the pipelined circuitswitching (PCS) communication mechanism[17]. Ariadne implements two virtual data channels and one virtual control channel per physical link. The router is self-timed with single flit buffering at the input and output ports, and is fully adaptive.

title: Efficiency Improvements for Signal's Handshake Protocol
abstract: Signal's handshake protocol non-interactively generates a shared key between two parties for secure communication. The underlying protocol X3DH, on which the post-quantum hybrid successor, PQXDH, builds, computes three to four individual Diffie-Hellman (DH) keys by combining the long-term identity keys and the ephemeral secrets of the two parties. Each of these DH operations serves a different purpose, either to authenticate the derived key or to provide forward secrecy.
keyword: Signal, X3DH, PQXDH, Diffie-Hellman, Efficiency Improvement

title: Brief Announcement: Delay-Optimal Transaction Order Fairness
abstract: Order-fair consensus aims to prevent a leader or block producer from exploiting transaction order, a concern amplified by front-running and MEV in decentralized finance. Existing order-fairness notions avoid some impossibilities by batching cyclic dependencies or by allowing bounded displacement, but these relaxations do not distinguish a tiny timing inversion from a large physical time gap. We revisit approximate-order-fairness (AOF), originally introduced and dismissed as too weak or impossible in prior work, in a synchronous model where parties can timestamp transaction arrivals using physical time. We show that time-aware AOF has a nontrivial feasible region: if a fraction � of nodes receive tx at least ? before tx', then tx can be forced before tx' whenever ? > ? sync / k and � > 1 - h/k , where h is the honest fraction and ? sync is the honest dissemination bound. We also give matching-style infeasibility constructions showing why smaller delays or lower thresholds permit Condorcet cycles. Finally, we outline how a HotStuff-style consensus layer can agree on timestamp reports while a deterministic ordering function enforces the strongest acyclic AOF constraints available in the observed execution.
keyword: Byzantine consensus, order fairness, transaction ordering, MEV

title: Quantitative analysis of the information content of use case diagrams using the objectified FBS metric based on normalized entropy
abstract: The article is an extended version of the poster published in ISD 2024 conference:
keyword: UML diagram metric, normalized entropy, use cases, software design

title: Session Summary Podcast: Session 16: AI in Healthcare Communication
abstract: An AI-generated podcast companion article to augment the AI in Healthcare Communication Session of the DIS '26

title: HappyCal: Designing Text and Image-Based Supports for Savouring Positive Work Experiences
abstract: Savouring positive work experiences can promote positive affect and well-being at work, yet there is limited guidance on how digital applications can support workers to engage in savouring. We developed HappyCal , a work-focused savouring application offering two forms of savouring support: text-based, a common modality in workplace reflection tools, and images, a largely unexplored approach in work-related savouring. We conducted an exploratory qualitative study where participants (N=36) used HappyCal over five days and engaged in savouring through either a text-only modality (n=17) or text input paired with image output (n=19). We found that (1) participants in both groups reported heightened awareness of work-related emotions through positive reflection, (2) Text-based support fostered conscious emotional processing, while image-based support offered quick overviews and amplified the positive experience, and (3) image-based support introduced a sense of playfulness into savouring. Informed by our results, we discuss implications for designing savouring supporting technologies for work contexts.
keyword: Savouring, Design, Positive Computing, Work

title: Internet of Things (IoT) Wearable Biosensors and Digital Infrastructure for Children's Health Camps: KasabaKiat Digital system
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT)?based digital health technologies, these wearable biosensor systems create significant diagnostic and monitoring advantages, including real-time feedback as critical data points for continuous assessment. The main objective of the present research is to provide a detailed modeling framework of the relationships among participants from various age and activity groups living in eco-digital health-camp environments, who have used IoT wearable biosensors. The aim of this study is to compare the differences in vital-sign variability, behavioral adaptation patterns, and their correlations in digital-green settings?KasabaKiat rural, KasabaKiat suburban, and KasabaKiat urban. We found more than 350 monitoring cases, including heart-rate fluctuations, respiratory rate anomalies, temperature variations, sleep-cycle orders, hydration levels, motion-pattern irregularities, and stress-response indicators. MIMIC-SEM analysis of multi-level time-structured sensor datasets among monitored children in different camp conditions, the digital clusters, interaction nodes, and latent constructs was significant and consistent. Vector Auto-Regression (VAR) analysis, including Granger causality tests and forecasting of the level of autonomic balance and psychophysiological coherence, is routinely applied in all KasabaKiat monitoring cycles to track adaptive responses. Some differences are observed in data integration methods, accuracy of sensor calibration, and camp-specific environmental conditions. Hence, we issue a recommendation to policymakers and educators, highlighting the need for more interdisciplinary data fusion and cross-system interoperability, and greater ethical transparency and data-governance standardization at the institutional, regional, and national levels aimed at improving child health management and ensuring the sustainability of the KasabaKiat digital ecosystem.

title: Vast, Low-Cost Honeypot Architecture
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost honeypot architecture designed to assist cybersecurity researchers and practitioners in collecting high-quality threat data using legacy equipment and open-source tools. By reusing older capital expense (CAPEX) devices and leveraging underutilized Internet Protocol (IP) and port resources, this framework enables the scaling of honeypot deployments across a wide range of interaction levels without requiring significant new investment. This paper outlines a flexible approach that combines virtualization, containerization, and scripting to build segmented environments capable of capturing both opportunistic and targeted attacks. The design includes the Principle of Least Purchase (PoLP), a practical strategy for converting surplus infrastructure into a valuable defense asset. We also provide a simple model for estimating attacker behavior across an expanded attack surface.

title: Towards a Decentralized and Privacy-Preserving Quality of Experience System for 6G Networks
abstract: The transition to 6G networks is expected to support a broader range of user-centric applications. As these applications expand, Quality of Experience (QoE) has emerged as a key metric for evaluating user satisfaction. However, the use of centralized systems lacks transparency and limits users? ability to govern their data usage. It also introduces challenges in managing QoE data while preserving privacy. At the same time, verification mechanisms are needed that allow regulators to evaluate compliance without exposing confidential business information. To address this, we propose a decentralized, privacy-preserving QoE system that integrates blockchain with fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This design enables transparent evaluations between users and service providers by supporting computations directly on encrypted data, ensuring that all information remains protected throughout the process. Users contribute QoE metrics through a decentralized infrastructure and retain control over their data. Regulators can monitor compliance without accessing raw data, and service providers can use encrypted QoE data to perform privacy-preserving computations via smart contracts without relying on a central authority. We developed a proof-of-concept integrating FHE smart contracts compatible with Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) blockchains and evaluated their performance using a video streaming dataset. Our results show that encryption and FHE operations consistently occur within milliseconds when tested in a local environment. We also evaluated these operations on a public blockchain testnet. In this setting, our system adds a millisecond-scale delay while supporting privacy-preserving computations directly on encrypted user data.
keyword: Blockchain, Quality of Experience, Privacy, Encryption, Decentralization

title: Safe But Not Sorry: Reducing Over-Conservatism in Safety Critics via Uncertainty-Aware Modulation
abstract: Ensuring safe exploration in reinforcement learning is essential for real-world deployment. Existing methods, however, often trade safety for performance by producing overly conservative policies or diffuse cost estimates that weaken policy gradients. We propose the Uncertain Safety Critic (USC), which modulates conservatism using critic uncertainty and refines under-covered regions, reducing safety violations by approx 40% while maintaining competitive or higher rewards and cutting cost-gradient error by approx 83%.
keyword: safe reinforcement learning, safety critics, safety-critical systems

title: The Evolving Battlefield: A Data-Driven Machine Learning Method for Identifying and Alleviating Contemporary DDoS Attacks
abstract: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks have evolved into multi-vector threats exploiting volumetric, protocol, and application layers, rendering traditional signature and threshold-based defenses increasingly ineffective. This study develops a machine learning (ML)- driven detection framework using modern datasets such as CICDDoS2019 to address zero-day threats, minimize false positives, and detect stealthy low-rate attacks. The pipeline incorporates pre-processing, feature optimization, and class balancing, applying models including Random Forest, Isolation Forest, Auto encoders, LSTM, and CNN. Evaluation with precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC confirms significant improvements in detection accuracy and resilience in imbalanced traffic conditions. Integration with adaptive mitigation tools such as WAFs, CDNs, and BGP Flow spec enables near real-time, context-aware filtering without disrupting legitimate traffic. Experimental results demonstrate enhanced detection speed, scalability, and accuracy, proving that ML-based behavioral analysis can outperform conventional methods and deliver robust, automated defenses against evolving DDoS strategies in high-speed, heterogeneous network environments. Using Apache Spark's distributed in- memory computations, we attained 99.5% accuracy, with faster training (14.08 min) and testing (0.04 min) compared to non-big data methods? slower performance.
keyword: Auto Encoders, Convolutional Neural Network, Distributed Denial-of-Service, Pre-Processing, Random Forest, machine learning

title: An Anonymous Cross-Domain Authentication Scheme Based on Blockchain Smart Contracts
abstract: To address the issues of excessive centralization and difficulties in cross-domain identity authentication in traditional cross-domain authentication schemes, an anonymous cross-domain authentication framework based on blockchain smart contracts is proposed. The framework uses Pedersen commitments to construct non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs, enabling users to achieve anonymous identity authentication with low communication overhead. Blockchain smart contracts are employed to record information about users and domains, realizing decentralized information storage. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme effectively reduces the level of centralization in cross-domain authentication and improves both the efficiency and security of cross-domain identity authentication.
keyword: Blockchain, Cross-domain Authentication, Privacy Protection, Smart- Contract

title: Geolocating Photovoltaic Systems using Geometry and Weather Data Correlation
abstract: With the increasing deployments of residential photovoltaic systems, successful attacks on photovoltaic inverters pose a threat to the stability of the power grid. If attackers with remote control over many inverters want to target segments of a power grid, they require knowledge of their location. To enable the development of countermeasures, we analyze how precisely inverters can be localized. We present two approaches to determine the location of an inverter, requiring only historical power generation data from each photovoltaic system. The first approach estimates times of equal solar elevation over multiple days, which uniquely identify a location through some astronomic and geometric observations. The second approach uses the correlation of daily differences in power generation with changes in local weather by measuring similarity to publicly available irradiation data. Both approaches are evaluated against real generation data from 1.428 photovoltaic systems, obtained from pvoutput.org, in a diverse set of scenarios. The first approach achieves a median spatial error of 108?km, while the second attains a median error of only 6?km. Given the broad range and rather low quality of the input data used, we achieve an accuracy that significantly exceeds existing research, even outperforming most previous results that use much higher quality input data. Multiple limiting factors are also identified, leaving opportunities for future work to further improve both approaches. The algorithms described in the present work are open-source.
keyword: Photovoltaic Systems, Inverter Geolocation, Solar Elevation Fitting, Weather Data Correlation, PV Power Generation Analysis, Solar Position Algorithm, Celestial Solar Tracking, Time-Series Analysis for Geolocation, Cybersecurity, Inverter-based Resources

title: InferenceProfiler: Enhancing the Observability of Performance, Cost, and Energy of LLM Inferencing in the Cloud
abstract: The widespread deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires substantial computational resources, often resulting in high operational costs and energy consumption. Optimizing these complex workloads necessitates precise visibility into how hardware accelerators and host system resources are utilized. This paper presents InferenceProfiler, a software tool that measures and records the resource usage of LLM inferencing tasks. Inference-Profiler is designed to profile the CPU/GPU, memory, disk, network, and power utilization of various tasks, collecting system metrics from the virtual machine (host), cgroup, process, GPU, and inference engine. InferenceProfiler leverages the NVIDIA Management Library (NVML) to capture real-time metrics across varying NVIDIA GPU architectures. InferenceProfiler integrates with vLLM, an open-source high-throughput inference engine for serving LLMs, to correlate application-level telemetry directly with underlying metrics. InferenceProfiler supports time-series profiling to enable continuous monitoring of the resources consumed by LLM inference.
keyword: large language models, LLM inferencing, performance profiling, observability, energy efficiency, cloud cost analysis

title: A typology of explanations to support Explainability-by-Design
abstract: As automated decision-making permeates almost all aspects of everyday life, capabilities to generate meaningful explanations for various stakeholders (i.e., decision-makers, addressees of decisions including individuals, auditors, and regulators) should be carefully deployed. This article presents a typology of explanations intended to support the first pillar of an explainability-by-design strategy. Its production has been achieved by pursuing a responsible innovation approach and introducing a new persona within the research and innovation process, i.e., a legal engineer, whose role is to work at the interface of two teams, the compliance and the engineering teams, and to oversee the process of requirement elicitation, which is often opinionated and narrowing. Once explanation requirements have been derived from applicable regulatory requirements, compliance rules, or business policies, they have been mapped to the dimensions of the typology to produce fine-grained explanation requirements, forming computable building blocks that can then be translated into system requirements during the technical design phase. The typology has been co-created with industry partners operating in two sectors: finance and education. Two pilot studies have thus been conducted to test both the feasibility of the generation and computation of explanations on the basis of the typology and the usefulness of the outputs in the light of the state-of-the-art. The typology comprises nine hierarchical dimensions. It can be leveraged to operate a stand-alone classifier of explanations that acts as detective controls within a broader partially automated compliance strategy. A machine-readable format of the typology is provided in the form of a light ontology.
keyword: Artificial intelligence, explainability, typology, data protection, automated decisions

title: Natural Language Processing Modeling for Content Mining and Sentiment Analysis in Online Media
abstract: The problems of word sense ambiguity and complex sentiment expression recognition in social media text sentiment analysis need to be solved urgently. By designing an analysis system based on improved BiLSTM-Attention, combined with an expanded sentiment lexicon, an optimized attention mechanism and domain knowledge, the complex sentiment recognition capability is greatly enhanced. Experimental results show that the system achieves 91.2% classification accuracy on the standard test set, and 86.7% and 89.3% accuracy in complex sentiment expressions and domain-specific phrase recognition, respectively. The system has been validated in several real-world application scenarios and provides new ideas for social media sentiment analysis.
keyword: BiLSTM-Attention, Deep Learning, Sentiment Analysis, Social Media

title: Chain of Evidence: Pixel-Level Visual Attribution for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation (iRAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for answering complex multi-hop questions by progressively retrieving and reasoning over external documents. However, current systems predominantly operate on parsed text, which creates two critical bottlenecks: (1) Coarse-grained attribution, where users are burdened with manually locating evidence within lengthy documents based on vague text-level citations; and (2) Visual semantic loss, where the conversion of visually rich documents (e.g., slides, PDFs with charts) into text discards spatial logic and layout cues essential for reasoning. To bridge this gap, we present Chain of Evidence (CoE), a retriever-agnostic visual attribution framework that leverages Vision-Language Models to reason directly over screenshots of retrieved document candidates. CoE eliminates format-specific parsing and outputs precise bounding boxes, visualizing the complete reasoning chain within the retrieved candidate set. We evaluate CoE on two distinct benchmarks: Wiki-CoE, a large-scale dataset of structured web pages derived from 2WikiMultiHopQA, and SlideVQA, a challenging dataset of presentation slides featuring complex diagrams and free-form layouts. Experiments demonstrate that fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct achieves robust performance, significantly outperforming text-based baselines in scenarios requiring visual layout understanding, while establishing a retriever-agnostic solution for pixel-level interpretable iRAG. Our code is available at https://github.com/PeiYangLiu/CoE.git.
keyword: multihop question answering, retrieval augmented generation, source attribution

title: Neo-antigen prediction using Mixture of Experts for HLA-peptides interactions with multi-factors incorporated
abstract: Accurate prediction of Neo-antigens is a fundamental task in cancer immunotherapy, requiring models capable of jointly modeling diverse biological signals. We introduce a Mixture of Experts (MoE)-based framework that integrates binding affinity, antigen processing, and presentation scores to predict peptide?HLA (pHLA) immunogenicity. In our approach, each allele?peptide pair is first encoded using an attention-enhanced bidirectional LSTM network, which captures both long-range sequence dependencies and localized contextual interactions. The resulting sequence representations are then combined with biological features through an MoE layer, where specialized expert networks are optimized to focus on distinct aspects of the Neo-antigen presentation process. A gating mechanism adaptively selects and weights the contributions of these experts, enabling robust feature fusion. The final integrated representation is used for binary classification of Neo-antigen presence. Empirical evaluations show that the proposed model achieves improved predictive performance over conventional single-stream architectures, highlighting the effectiveness of MoE in handling heterogeneous feature spaces for immunogenicity prediction. Moreover, the framework is flexible and can be extended to incorporate additional immunological signals, such as eluted ligands or T-cell receptor recognition features, further enhancing its applicability to Neo-antigen discovery.
keyword: Neo-antigen prediction, Mixture of Experts (MoE), MHC class I, Binding affinity, Antigen processing, Presentation score

title: Research on the Architecture of a Digital Extracurricular Platform for Cultivating Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competencies
abstract: Extracurricular activities are an essential part of a well-rounded education at higher education institutions, yet traditional management methods are inefficient and wasteful. This paper presents a digital extracurricular platform based on a front-end/back-end separation architecture. This comprehensive system encompasses core functionalities such as user management, activity management and credit certification. The platform uses a RESTful interface design and multi-layered security protection mechanisms to fully digitise activity management processes. Research findings suggest that digital transformation can greatly improve the efficiency of extracurricular programme management and the user experience, providing valuable insights for the development of university extracurricular programmes.
keyword: Credit certification, Digital management, Extracurricular programs, Frontend-backend separation, RESTful interfaces

title: Are Covert DDoS Attacks Facing Multi-Feature Detectors Feasible?
abstract: We state and prove the square root scaling laws for the amount of traffic injected by a covert attacker into a network from a set of homes under the assumption that traffic descriptors follow a multivariate Gaussian distribution. We numerically evaluate the obtained result under realistic settings wherein traffic is collected from real users, leveraging detectors that exploit multiple features. Under such circumstances, we observe that phase transitions predicted by the model still hold.

title: SAER: Scalable Assessment of E-commerce Recommendations using Large Language Models
abstract: Selecting which recommendation algorithm variant to advance to online experimentation is a critical decision in industry practice. Manual evaluation is subjective and time-consuming, while offline metrics such as nDCG often fail to correlate with real-world customer preferences. We present SAER, a two-stage framework (pointwise filtering and pairwise comparison) that uses Large Language Models as judges to evaluate e-commerce recommendation quality. For pointwise evaluation, SAER achieves higher agreement with human consensus (? w = 0.58) than human annotators achieve with each other (? w = 0.38). For pairwise evaluation, SAER mitigates position bias (88.0% consistency) and demonstrates strong adversarial robustness (91.0% detection rate). In a large-scale online case study serving over 10M impressions, the algorithm SAER preferred offline also achieved a statistically significant click-through rate (CTR) lift ( p < 0.0001), providing encouraging directional evidence, though this single observation cannot establish a general predictive relationship. SAER produces reproducible, explainable signals in approximately 30 minutes for $28, positioning it as a scalable pre-screening layer for recommendation development.
keyword: recommendation systems, large language models, llm-as-a-judge, evaluation metrics, e-commerce, prompt engineering, a/b testing

title: How Practitioners Assess Software System Security
abstract: Despite progress in software security, there is still a limited understanding of how to measure and evaluate it comprehensively. However, developers and security analysts have to regularly assess software security and respond to issues. To shed light on their practices and perceptions, in this work, we qualitatively investigate how practitioners assess software security and make related decisions.
keyword: software security assessments, security risk, vulnerabilities, human studies

title: Method of moments for Gaussian mixtures: Implementation and benchmarks
abstract: Gaussian mixture models are universal approximators in the sense that any smooth density can be approximated arbitrarily well with a Gaussian mixture model with enough components. Due to their broad expressive power, Gaussian mixture models appear in many applications. As a result, algebraic parameter recovery for Gaussian mixture models from data is a valuable contribution to multiple fields. Our work documents performance of the method of moments for high dimensional Gaussian mixtures. We outline the method of moments, and selections of moments and their corresponding polynomials that work well for parameter recovery in practice. Our main contribution puts these ideas into practice with an implementation as a julia package, GMMParameterEstimation , as well as computational benchmarks.

title: Investigating Design Considerations for Supporting Remote Teaching and Learning of Physical Drawing
abstract: Teaching and learning physical drawing remotely pose user-experience challenges. In an online physical drawing course, instructors must interact with students through a camera for demonstrations, supervision, communication, and annotations in real-time. However, these activities are not well supported by commonly used video conferencing services. We conduct a qualitative study with seven instructors and five students to understand their practices and challenges in teaching and learning of physical drawing in a remote setting. Our study identifies four design considerations that a system supporting remote teaching and learning of physical drawing should take into account. We then demonstrate the technical feasibility of these design considerations by building a working prototype called SharedCanvas. We also validate our design considerations through a user study with SharedCanvas, revealing how they better supported interactions between instructors and students. We conclude by discussing our work in light of related studies on online drawing education and present future research opportunities to improve remote teaching of drawing.
keyword: Remote teaching and learning, design considerations, physical drawing

title: Federated Learning for Smart Homes: A Review of Architecture, Privacy Protection, and Personalization Approaches
abstract: Smart homes generate vast amounts of sensitive user data, but using that data often comes at the cost of privacy. Federated learning offers a way out by keeping data on devices and only sharing model updates. This review looks at how federated learning is being adapted for smart homes from three angles?system design, privacy protection, and personalization. We compare different architectural choices, weigh the pros and cons of existing privacy techniques, and take a close look at how researchers are tackling the challenge of data heterogeneity. Our goal is to give a clear, grounded picture of where the field stands and where it?s headed.
keyword: Federated Learning, Smart Home, Privacy Protection

title: Adaptive Gait Biometrics for Real Time Continuous Authentication
abstract: This paper presents a continuous authentication system that leverages gait analysis by integrating real-time image processing and machine learning to overcome the vulnerabilities of traditional one-time verification methods. Utilizing gait?a natural, spoof-resistant biometric?the framework enables non-intrusive, real-time identity validation. A Microsoft Kinect sensor captures 3D kinematic features (speed, stride length, joint angles), which are processed by machine learning models to authenticate users against pre-trained profiles. The system dynamically adapts to environmental variables (lighting, terrain) and mitigates gait variability (e.g., injuries) via confidence-based early stopping, thereby optimizing computational efficiency. Privacy is maintained through encrypted data storage and processing. Evaluations reveal robust performance in controlled settings and scalability for high-security applications such as access control. Although accuracy is promising, challenges persist in heterogeneous environments, underscoring the need for multi-sensor integration. This work advances gait biometrics by balancing security and usability, offering a passive authentication solution that enhances convenience while protecting against impersonation threats.
keyword: Gait Analysis, Continuous Authentication, Machine Learning, Secure Access Control

title: A Prompt-Aware Structuring Framework for Reliable Reuse of AI-Generated Content in the Agentic Web
abstract: The evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) and the software agents built on them (AI agents) marks a turning point in the transition from a human-centric Web to an ''Agentic Web'' driven by AI agents. However, for AI-Generated Content (AIGC), which is expected to dominate the Web, there is currently no mechanism for agents to verify its reliability, reproducibility, or license compliance during generation. This lack of transparency risks causing chained hallucinations and compliance violations through the reuse of AIGC. Consequently, a framework to manage the provenance and generation conditions of AIGC is essential. In this paper, we present a framework that automatically attaches structured metadata to AIGC at generation time, including modularized prompts, contexts, thoughts, model information, hyperparameters, and confidence. The metadata is enveloped together with verifiable credentials to support the reliable assessment and reuse of AIGC. This framework enables efficient curation of structured AIGC and facilitates its safe use for applications such as fine-tuning and knowledge distillation.
keyword: agentic web, fine-tuning, llm distillation, structured metadata

title: Brief Announcement: Computing Least Fixed Points with Overwrite Semantics in Parallel and Distributed Systems
abstract: We present methods to compute least fixed points of multiple monotone inflationary functions in parallel and distributed settings. While the classic Knaster-Tarski theorem addresses a single function with sequential iteration, modern computing systems require parallel execution with overwrite semantics, non-atomic updates, and stale reads. We prove three convergence theorems under progressively relaxed synchronization: (1) Interleaving semantics with fair scheduling, (2) Parallel execution with update-only-on-change semantics (processes write only on those coordinates whose values change), and (3) Distributed execution with bounded staleness (updates propagate within T rounds) and i -locality (each process modifies only its own component).
keyword: fixed points, distributive lattices, parallel algorithms, asynchronous computation, overwrite semantics, bounded staleness

title: Quantum-Safe, Efficient, and AI-Enhanced Blockchains for the Web: A Cooperative Tutorial on Quantum Computing, Blockchain Applications, and Data Standards
abstract: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized groundbreaking advances in quantum information science, underscoring the transformative potential of quantum technologies for computation and communication. As these developments accelerate, they simultaneously pose profound challenges to classical cryptographic foundations?particularly the public-key algorithms securing blockchain systems, digital signatures, and distributed consensus. However, despite the clear urgency to address quantum-induced vulnerabilities, the translation of theoretical quantum computing breakthroughs from laboratory research into robust, real-world applications for blockchain security remains limited. Building on this momentum, our tutorial explores how quantum computing and blockchain can jointly redefine the trust, efficiency, and intelligence of next-generation Web systems. We introduce the principles of quantum computing and their implications for secure, scalable blockchain architectures, emphasizing post-quantum and quantum-assisted cryptography. The tutorial situates these technologies within broader contexts of privacy, human?computer interaction, and ethical data governance, highlighting how interdisciplinary collaboration across computer science, economics, and human-centered computing can enable a more trustworthy Web. We further discuss how quantum techniques can enhance computational efficiency, randomness, and resilience for decentralized systems, while open data standards provide a foundation for transparency, interoperability, and reproducibility. The session culminates in an immersive experience where participants engage with cloud-based quantum computation through Amazon Braket, comparing multiple quantum backends to witness firsthand how such tools advance secure and efficient blockchain innovation. By integrating insights from quantum computing, blockchain applications, and artificial intelligence, the session provides a forward-looking roadmap toward building trust and intelligence for a quantum-ready internet.
keyword: quantum computing, post-quantum cryptography (pqc), blockchain security, distributed web, artificial intelligence, quantum-assisted learning, open data and standards, metadata interoperability, reproducibility, web3 interoperability, quantum cloud computing, data governance and responsible ai, quantum-ready web systems

title: Numerical simulation study of elastic plate impacted by water column based on FEM-KGF-DSPH
abstract: Research is carried out around the FEM-KGF-DSPH coupling algorithm for simulating the fluid-solid coupling problem. For the FEM-KGF-DSPH fluid-solid coupling algorithm, the computational accuracies of the traditional SPH and KGF-DSPH methods are compared and verified, and high-precision numerical simulations of the water column impacting on an elastic plate are carried out. The results show that FEM-KGF-DSPH satisfies the advantage of SPH in dealing with large deformation of fluids, and meets the requirements of FEM in simulating the deformation accuracy of elastomers. This paper provides a good computational fluid dynamics method for high-precision numerical simulation of fluid-solid coupling.
keyword: Finite element method, elastic plate, simulation, smooth particle hydrodynamics method, water column

title: Satellite Imagery Processing using NDVI for the Detection of Illegal Mining in Chaspa, Puno - Peru
abstract: Peru is a country that distributes its economic activity in the export of oil, natural gas, precious metals and mining, the latter being often extracted illegally, which causes havoc and damage to a certain geographical area. The Peruvian jungle and high Andean areas are areas of difficult access, where the communication signal is poor, this can cause that the authorities fail to supervise and control efficiently, therefore, illegal mining often expands damaging the environment, for this reason it is proposed remote monitoring of the area of Chaspa, Puno using satellite images. In this research, an image processing algorithm using NDVI was developed to locate the damages done in that geographical area from the year 2017 to 2022. The implementation of the algorithm was performed using computer vision, employing an EarthExplorer Data Set and LANDSAT 7 satellite images. Achieving the detection of the variation in vegetation in the period 2017 - 2022 by means of coloration indicators. This algorithm can be taken as a reference to analyze other places affected by illegal mining or even to map new areas as a future projection, these images can be derived to jurisdictional entities for their respective action and contribution to the improvement and reduction of illegal mining in Peru or in other countries.
keyword: NDVI, deforestation, illegal mining, image processing

title: Sampling Parallelism for Fast and Efficient Bayesian Learning
abstract: Machine learning models, and deep neural networks in particular, are increasingly deployed in risk-sensitive domains such as healthcare, environmental forecasting, and finance, where reliable quantification of predictive uncertainty is essential. However, many uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods remain difficult to apply due to their substantial computational cost. Sampling-based Bayesian learning approaches, such as Bayesian neural networks (BNNs), are particularly expensive since drawing and evaluating multiple parameter samples rapidly exhausts memory and compute resources. These constraints have limited the accessibility and exploration of Bayesian techniques thus far. To address these challenges, we introduce sampling parallelism, a simple yet powerful parallelization strategy that targets the primary bottleneck of sampling-based Bayesian learning: the samples themselves. By distributing sample evaluations across multiple GPUs, our method reduces memory pressure and training time without requiring architectural changes or extensive hyperparameter tuning. We detail the methodology and evaluate its performance on a few example tasks and architectures, comparing against distributed data parallelism (DDP) as a baseline. We further demonstrate that sampling parallelism is complementary to existing strategies by implementing a hybrid approach that combines sample and data parallelism. Our experiments show near-perfect scaling when the sample number is scaled proportionally to the computational resources, confirming that sample evaluations parallelize cleanly. Although DDP achieves better raw speedups under scaling with constant workload, sampling parallelism has a notable advantage: by applying independent stochastic augmentations to the same batch on each GPU, it increases augmentation diversity and thus reduces the number of epochs required for convergence.
keyword: Parallel Computing, Uncertainty Quantification, Neural Networks

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Multi-Class Emotion Recognition in English Social Media Text: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis
abstract: Emotion recognition from social media text has emerged as a critical task in natural language processing with applications spanning mental health monitoring, customer sentiment analysis, and human-computer interaction. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of classical machine learning and deep learning approaches for multi-class emotion classification in English Twitter text. We systematically evaluate six distinct models?Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, CNN, BiLSTM, and CNN-LSTM hybrid architecture?on a dataset comprising six emotion categories: sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, and surprise. Our preprocessing pipeline integrates lexical normalization, morphological processing, and dual feature representation strategies using TF-IDF for traditional models and sequence embedding for neural architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN achieves the highest performance with 91.45% test accuracy and a mean AUC of 0.992, significantly outperforming traditional approaches. The hybrid CNN-LSTM model, while computationally more complex, achieves only 45.6% accuracy, suggesting that architectural complexity does not guarantee superior performance for this task. Our analysis reveals that joy and sadness are the most reliably classified emotions across all models, while surprise remains challenging due to its semantic similarity with other emotional states. This work provides empirical evidence for the effectiveness of convolutional architectures in capturing local emotional patterns in short social media text.
keyword: BiLSTM, CNN, deep learning, emotion recognition, natural language processing, sentiment analysis, social media analysis

title: BeLink: Biomedical Entity Linking Meets Generative Re-Ranking
abstract: Despite recent progress, Biomedical Entity Linking (BEL) with large language models (LLMs) remains computationally inefficient and challenging to deploy in practical settings. In this work, we demonstrate that instruction-tuning of open-source generative models can offer an effective solution when applied at the re-ranking stage of the BEL pipeline. We propose a set-wise instruction-tuning formulation that enables fast and accurate candidate selection. Our method demonstrates strong performance on multiple BEL benchmarks, yielding significant improvements in linking accuracy (3%?24%) while reducing inference time compared to the state-of-the-art. We integrate our generative re-ranker into BeLink, a modular, end-to-end system designed for practical real-world BEL applications.
keyword: entity linking, concept normalization, concept recognition, retrieval-augmented generation, query reformulation, generative re-ranking

title: Visualization Analysis of Teaching Reform in Advanced Mathematics Based on Knowledge Graphs
abstract: This study presents a computational and visualization-based analysis of 767 academic publications on Advanced Mathematics curriculum reform from 2015 to 2025. To address the limitations of traditional qualitative reviews, this research constructs a data-driven analytical framework integrating natural language processing, network science, and knowledge graph visualization. Text preprocessing and TF?IDF weighting were employed to extract representative keywords. A weighted cooccurrence network was constructed and analyzed using Louvain community detection, centrality measures, and Fruchterman?Reingold graph layouts. Temporal patterns were modeled using Kleinberg's burst detection algorithm to capture emerging research trends.The results reveal a fragmented yet evolving research structure, with several high-degree hubs and nine well-defined thematic clusters. Temporal analysis identifies shifts in research priorities, including long-term emphasis on curriculum ideological and political education and medium-term growth in technology-enhanced teaching. This study contributes a reproducible computational framework for educational knowledge graph analysis and demonstrates the effectiveness of graph-based methods in uncovering structural and temporal patterns in large-scale academic corpora.
keyword: Burst Detection, Educational Data Mining, Knowledge Graphs, Louvain Algorithm, TF?IDF, Visualization Analytics

title: Google's Original Secret Sauce: The PageRank Algorithm
abstract: In this teaching tip and courseware note, we describe a series of in-class exercises and homework assignments that we've used to introduce the PageRank algorithm to a wide range of students, from high school to non-majors, to students majoring in CS and IS. These exercises range in complexity from simulating the PageRank algorithm on a spreadsheet to implementing the algorithm with the MapReduce paradigm on the Spark big data platform. Student feedback on the pedagogical value of these exercises in highlighting the nuances and beauty of the PageRank algorithm has been very positive.
keyword: pagerank, mapreduce, spark

title: Research on Innovation Paths and Resource Optimization in International Chinese Language Education Empowered by Artificial Intelligence
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), new opportunities with emerged for reshaping international Chinese language education. AI technologies for intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms, natural language processing in multimodal interaction provide innovative tools that enhance teaching efficiency, learning personalization in cross-cultural communication. The study explores the innovation paths through which AI empowers international Chinese education, focusing on curriculum design, intelligent resource development in learner-centered pedagogical models. At the same time, it examines strategies for optimizing resource allocation, utilized the integration of digital platforms, cloud-based learning environments in data-driven assessment mechanisms, has address existing issues of uneven distribution at low utilization of educational resources. By combining theoretical analysis with practical cases, the research highlights how AI can improve teaching effectiveness, expat access to high-quality resources in promote sustainable development in international Chinese education. The findings provide a reference for policymakers, educators in technology developers seeking to build an intelligent, inclusive in globally connected ecosystem for Chinese language learning.
keyword: Artificial Intelligence, Innovation Paths, Intelligent Learning, International Chinese Language Education, Resource Optimization

title: Multi-Attribute Committee Selection: Diversity, Correlation, and Approximation Guarantees
abstract: We study the problem of multi-attribute committee selection, where each candidate is described by categorical attributes and the objective is to match a given target distribution over these attributes. Building on the framework of Lang and Skowron [2], we formalize and analyze the L p class of voting rules, including the well-studied Hamilton rule representing L p .
keyword: computational social choice, multiwinner voting

title: Identifying master transcriptional regulators with single-cell-based networks
abstract: Master transcriptional regulators are small sets of transcription factors that drive or inhibit cell differentiation. Discovering these master regulators has high clinical importance, as this knowledge can guide cellular reprogramming. However, this is a highly challenging task, as many master regulators do not show significant expression change across cell states, but their activity can be altered due to the changes in the epigenetic landscape of the cell.
keyword: master transcriptional regulators, single-cell multiome, cellular reprogramming, transcriptional regulatory networks, gene regulation

topic: Collaborative and social computing theory, concepts and paradigms
title: Broken Links and Fading Stories: How Dominant Online Platforms Subvert the Hypermedia Foundation of the Web
abstract: The World Wide Web was envisioned as an open, decentralized network of documents connected by hyperlinks. That architecture enabled a distributed, user-navigable information space grounded in link-based knowledge traversal. Today, dominant online platforms increasingly depart from this vision. By exploiting the Web?s non-functional properties and introducing architectures that constrain linking, limit navigation, and normalize ephemerality, platforms transform an open hypermedia environment into platform-governed silos. These design choices restrict users? ability to reference, verify, and preserve information, fracturing the Web?s connective fabric. In this adversarial situation, users adopt transcension practices?such as reposts, screenshots, and off-platform link hubs?to rebuild continuity and recover the Web?s original affordances. Yet these responses remain ad-hoc workarounds rather than structural correctives, revealing the growing tension between an open, interoperable Web on the one hand?and platform architectures optimized for containment, opacity, and control on the other. Drawing from Web architecture, hypermedia theory, and contemporary platform analysis, this paper examines how platforms subvert openness and leverage ephemerality to consolidate control over information flows, and how users? workaround practices simultaneously compensate for and mitigate these structural constraints. We argue and call for renewed commitment to foundational hypermedia principles and contend that reclaiming the hyperlink as a first-class architectural primitive is essential to preserving the Web?s role.
keyword: Web, Web Architecture, Hyperlinks, Ephemeral Content, Dominant Online Platforms, Walled Gardens

subfield_name: Human and societal aspects of security and privacy
title: Visual Privacy: The Impact of Privacy Labels on Privacy Behaviors Online
abstract: Research has consistently shown that websites? privacy policies fail to inform users, prompting to explore more condensed, visual solutions such as icons and privacy labels. However, we miss efficient and scalable systems to generate such privacy labels and conclusive evidence on their impact on people?s privacy protection behavior. This article fills these gaps: we present the Visual Privacy browser extension that automatically computes a privacy rating and visualizes it in a privacy label. We studied the impact of those labels on privacy protection behavior in an online experiment ( N =825). Our results show that the privacy labels shown by Visual Privacy significantly impact a website?s perceived risks and benefits, and that they have an indirect effect on privacy protection behavior. Study participants showed high awareness and acceptance of privacy labels, with 79% of participants recalling the rating shown in a label and over 75% reporting that they would like them to become mandatory.
keyword: Privacy labels, privacy policies, digital privacy, protection motivation theory, data protection, privacy-by-design

topic: Ubiquitous and mobile computing systems and tools
title: Short Paper: Towards Algorithmically Grounded Embedded AI Models
abstract: Embedded systems were once built with clarity?each line of code grounded in an algorithm, each behavior traceable and explainable. But as AI models rapidly replace classical methods in sensing, scheduling, decision, and control, we have gained accuracy at the cost of trust. Today?s neural networks are black boxes, assembled by intuition or brute force, leaving us unable to explain, debug, or control their behavior. We argue this is not just a tooling issue, but a design flaw: explainability has long been an afterthought, with networks built first and interpreted later. We advocate a principled approach where networks are grounded in algorithms and designed with internal anchors?expected intermediate behaviors, invariants, or interpretable signals?that support debugging and interpretation. This paper presents Algorithm-Informed Neural Networks (AINN)?architectures shaped by algorithms as implicit inductive bias. By decomposing algorithms into logic blocks, we build modular networks that are easier to train, interpret, and debug. As proof of concept, we present two use cases? fall detection keyword spotting problems?showing how algorithmic structure improves training efficiency and enables effective debugging.
keyword: Algorithm-informed Neural Networks, Explainable AI, Debuggable Neural Networks.

title: CXLMemSim: Practical Performance Simulation and Characterization of CXL 3.0 Memory Systems
abstract: Compute Express Link (CXL) 3.0 can turn stranded DRAM into a composable datacenter memory fabric, but hardware is scarce and cycle-accurate simulation is prohibitively slow for full workloads. CXLMemSim is an open-source software CXL memory simulator that keeps computation at native speed and models only CXL-affected memory behavior. Across SPEC CPU2017, Memcached, wrf, vector search, and llama.cpp, CXLMemSim stays within 11?15% of hardware and gem5 while completing a Redis-scale run in 45 minutes instead of gem5?s 73 hours. The public release at SlugLab/CXLMemSim provides PEBS/LBR/eBPF tracing, JSON topology descriptions, and reusable migration/cache policy hooks for CXL design-space exploration.
keyword: CXL, memory disaggregation, memory systems, simulation, performance modeling

title: CAPE's Composable Server Infrastructure for the Edge-Cloud Continuum: Invited Paper
abstract: The European project CAPE (European Open Compute Architecture for Powerful Edge) aims to develop composable, cognitive, and sustainable Cloud-Edge server infrastructures, completely based on open standards[ 6 ]. CAPE started in December 2024. The consortium includes 7�SMEs, 4�academic partners and the international standardization committee PICMG, with members from 7� countries. This paper presents the project?s current state and focuses on the eHPS hardware platform and the integration of the Compute Express Link (CXL) technology. On the software side, CAPE has a strong focus on application deployment and workflow orchestration on hybrid edge-cloud clusters. As an MVP for the software integration, we describe the automated bootstrapping of a Kubernetes-based edge-cloud cluster using the Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool Pulumi. The bootstrapping tools and other optional deployed applications, such as the openDesk stack and a variety of cluster-management and open-source development tools such as Prometheus/Grafana and GitLab, are available open-source�[ 18 ].
keyword: European Project, Edge-Cloud Continuum, CXL, Composable Server Infrastructure, Modular Microserver, COM-HPC, Heterogeneous Computing, Infrastructure from Code (IfC), Kubernetes, Orchestration

title: LLM-Augmented Conflict Prioritization and Strategy Selection for PCB Placement Refinement
abstract: Printed circuit board (PCB) layouts frequently undergo refinement due to engineering changes such as package updates and component substitutions. These changes often introduce localized placement conflicts that must be resolved efficiently while preserving the original layout topology. Existing refinement flows typically rely on rule-based conflict ranking and fixed repair sequences, which struggle to capture the functional importance and contextual impact of different conflicts under complex design scenarios. This paper presents an LLM-augmented framework for PCB placement refinement, in which an LLM is employed as a high-level decision layer for conflict prioritization and repair strategy selection. Detected placement conflicts are characterized using geometric severity, local congestion, component categories, and violation types. Based on these features, the LLM infers relative conflict priorities and selects appropriate repair strategies, while conventional placement heuristics are responsible for performing fine-grained geometric adjustments under impact-aware constraints. Experiments on diverse PCB datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach improves overall conflict resolution by about 15% and high-priority conflict resolution by over 20%, while maintaining practical computational efficiency.
keyword: PCB auto-placement, conflict prioritization, design rule checking, large language model

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Learning Path Optimization System for Rural Revitalization Talents
abstract: The in-depth implementation of the rural revitalization strategy has imposed higher requirements on the cultivation of interdisciplinary talents, while traditional one-size-fits-all educational models struggle to meet the personalized needs of learners from diverse backgrounds. This study constructs an adaptive learning path optimization system based on Deep Q-Network (DQN) that achieves personalized course recommendations and dynamic resource allocation through real-time perception of learners? knowledge states and intelligent prediction of learning behaviors. The system integrates knowledge graph technology to construct a knowledge system for the rural revitalization domain, encompassing 537 knowledge nodes and 1,243 relationship edges across four major themes: agricultural technology, economic management, ecological protection, and cultural heritage. A multi-objective reward mechanism is designed that encompasses learning effectiveness, time cost, and knowledge coverage. The Double DQN algorithm is employed to address overestimation problems in high-dimensional state spaces, with network training utilizing experience replay mechanisms and epsilon-greedy exploration strategies. Large-scale simulation experiments involving 5,000 virtual learners validate the system?s effectiveness across multiple evaluation metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to traditional recommendation algorithms including Random, Collaborative Filtering, and Q-learning methods, the proposed system achieves significant improvements: learning completion rate reaches 87.340% (32.180% improvement over Random), knowledge mastery level attains 0.823 (28.000% improvement), and time efficiency achieves 0.0456 points per hour. Ablation experiments confirm the necessity of knowledge graph constraints, multi-objective reward functions, experience replay mechanisms, and the Double DQN structure. The system demonstrates strong adaptability across different learner levels, with particularly significant support for beginner learners whose average knowledge mastery increased from 0.512 to 0.789, representing a 54.100% improvement. This research provides an intelligent solution for rural revitalization talent cultivation and offers methodological reference for personalized education and lifelong learning system design.
keyword: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Adaptive Learning Path, Rural Revitalization, Talent Cultivation, Personalized Education

title: Resilient Strategies for Stochastic Systems: How Much Does it Take to Break a Winning Strategy?
abstract: We study the problem of resilient strategies in the presence of uncertainty. Resilient strategies enable an agent to make decisions that are robust against disturbances. In particular, we are interested in those disturbances that are able to flip a decision made by the agent. Such a disturbance may, for instance, occur when the intended action of the agent cannot be executed due to a malfunction of an actuator in the environment. In this work, we introduce the concept of resilience in the stochastic setting and present a comprehensive set of fundamental problems.
